title: Fast Track vs Breakthrough Therapy vs RMAT vs Priority Review vs National Priority Voucher
summary: How Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, RMAT, Priority Review, and FDA's National Priority Voucher pilot change review in practice, with approval precedents.
body_markdown:
## FDA expedited programs in practice: Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, RMAT, Priority Review, and the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher


### The short answer


The four statutory expedited programs do different jobs. None of them lowers the approval standard.


- **Fast Track** gives you access: more frequent meetings and eligibility for rolling review[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=28)[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=41) .
- **Breakthrough Therapy designation (BTD)** adds intensive FDA involvement early in development, backed by an organizational commitment that includes senior managers[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=42) .
- **RMAT designation** gives regenerative medicine products all the BTD features on a lower evidentiary trigger. It also points more explicitly toward accelerated approval[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=85)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=29)[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=47) .
- **Priority Review** is a separate step. It shortens the review clock from 10 months to 6 months, and FDA assigns it at filing[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31)[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=269)[271](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=271) .


The Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot is newer, and FDA created it without a dedicated statute. It targets an action 1 to 2 months after the final submission. It gets there by front-loading CMC and labeling review and by running a team-based "tumor board" review[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests)[75](https://www.fda.gov/media/190896/download)[78](https://www.fda.gov/media/190927/download) . Early CNPV approvals have come in roughly 44 to 50 days after filing[59](https://pharmadossier.com/blog/fda-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program)[60](https://www.biospace.com/fda/9-months-in-fdas-new-priority-voucher-program-still-clouded-with-uncertainty)[416](https://crwepressrelease.com/press-release/12402/fda-approves-first-new-molecular-entity-under-national-priority-voucher-program) . The program has also produced at least one complete response[59](https://pharmadossier.com/blog/fda-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program) , and critics have questioned its legal basis and how products are selected[327](https://www.citizen.org/article/comments-to-the-fda-about-the-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-pilot-program/)[331](https://www.americanactionforum.org/insight/assessing-the-fdas-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-program/) .


### Side-by-side comparison


Program Qualifying standard What actually changes Request and FDA response


Fast Track Serious condition, plus nonclinical or clinical data showing potential to address an unmet medical need (QIDPs also eligible)[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=28)[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=36) Frequent interactions with the review team (pre-IND, end-of-phase 1, end-of-phase 2 meetings); possible rolling review; priority review possible if data support it at submission[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=28)[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=41) With the IND or later, ideally by the pre-NDA/BLA meeting; FDA responds within 60 calendar days[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31)[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=33)


Breakthrough Therapy Serious condition, plus preliminary clinical evidence that the drug may show substantial improvement over available therapy on a clinically significant endpoint[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=41)[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=36) All Fast Track features, plus intensive guidance from phase 1, senior-manager involvement, and a cross-disciplinary project lead where appropriate[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=42)[314](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=314) Ideally before efficacy trials start (by end-of-phase 2); FDA responds within 60 calendar days[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=38)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31)


RMAT (section 506(g)) Regenerative medicine therapy for a serious condition, plus preliminary clinical evidence of potential to address unmet medical need; no "substantial improvement" showing required[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=87)[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=85)[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=84) All BTD features; early interactions on surrogate or intermediate endpoints that could support accelerated approval; statutory attention to ways of meeting postapproval requirements[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=29)[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=47) With a new IND or an IND amendment to CBER; decision within 60 calendar days[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=84)[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=85)


Priority Review Serious condition, and a significant improvement in safety or effectiveness if approved; also triggered by statute (for example, priority review vouchers, QIDPs)[271](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=271)[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=36) Review goal of 6 months instead of 10 months; directs FDA attention and resources to the application[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31)[271](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=271)[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=269) Assigned at filing; applicant told by day 60[268](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=268)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31)


CNPV (pilot, June 2025) Fit with one or more of five "national priorities" (public health crisis, innovative therapy, large unmet need, onshoring, affordability)[74](https://www.fda.gov/industry/commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program)[81](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-proactively-awards-national-priority-voucher-based-strong-phase-3-study-results)[83](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-grants-two-national-priority-vouchers) Target action 1 to 2 months after final submission; CMC and labeling due 60 days before final submission; team-based review council[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests)[74](https://www.fda.gov/industry/commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program)[75](https://www.fda.gov/media/190896/download) Selected by FDA from internal nominations or sponsor submissions[75](https://www.fda.gov/media/190896/download)[78](https://www.fda.gov/media/190927/download)


### Fast Track: access, not acceleration by itself


The core guidance is still *Expedited Programs for Serious Conditions: Drugs and Biologics* (May 2014)[48](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=48) . What Fast Track actually gives you is more interaction with FDA. That includes pre-IND, end-of-phase 1, and end-of-phase 2 meetings covering study design, the safety database, dose-response, and biomarkers[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=28) . The second benefit is rolling review. If FDA's preliminary look at the clinical data suggests the product may be effective, FDA can start reviewing parts of the marketing application before the complete application arrives[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=41) .


Two limits matter in practice:


- Fast Track does not include priority review. It only makes the product eligible if the data at submission support it[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=28) .
- Accelerated approval is a separate pathway. FDA may discuss it with the sponsor during Fast Track interactions, but designation does not confer it[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=28)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31) .


FDA can rescind the designation if emerging data no longer support the unmet-need showing, or if the sponsor stops pursuing the designated program[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31)[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=38) .


**Scale.** CBER data from March 1998 through January 31, 2024 show 814 Fast Track requests, 581 granted and 218 denied[106](https://www.fda.gov/about-fda/center-biologics-evaluation-and-research-cber/fast-track-designation-request-performance) . Among CDER novel approvals, 22 of 50 in 2024 (44%) had Fast Track[108](https://www.fda.gov/files/drugs/published/new-drug-therapy-2025-annual-report.pdf) , as did 18 of 46 in 2025 (39%)[109](https://www.fda.gov/media/190705/download) .


### Breakthrough Therapy: how much FDA engages


BTD carries a higher bar. Sponsors need *clinical* evidence of a treatment effect that may be a substantial improvement over available therapy, generally from phase 1 or phase 2 trials. Mechanistic or nonclinical data alone are not enough[319](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=319) . A clinically significant endpoint can be:


- irreversible morbidity or mortality, or serious symptoms,
- an established surrogate endpoint,
- a surrogate reasonably likely to predict benefit, or
- a clearly better safety profile with similar efficacy[313](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=313)[314](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=314) .


BTD adds to Fast Track in three ways:


- intensive, interactive guidance from as early as phase 1, including discussion of adaptive, enrichment, crossover, or historically controlled designs[314](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=314)[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=42)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=29) ;
- intensive involvement of senior managers and experienced review staff[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=42) ;
- a cross-disciplinary project lead where appropriate[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=42) .


The benefit is front-loaded. FDA wants requests before the efficacy trials start, and it rarely sees them after a marketing application has been submitted[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=38)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31) .


BTD can be lost. If another drug gets traditional approval for the same use, the designated product generally keeps BTD only if it may still show substantial improvement over that newly approved drug. FDA gives the sponsor notice and a chance to argue for keeping the designation, and rescission does not rule out eventual approval[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=41)[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=321) .


**Precedents from Drugs@FDA review files.** These records show BTD, Fast Track, rolling review, and priority review used together:


- **Cabometyx (cabozantinib), NDA 208692.** Fast Track was granted April 8, 2015, and BTD August 21, 2015. The rolling NDA began October 13, 2015, and the final clinical component was submitted December 22, 2015. The application was reviewed as Priority and has a decision date of April 25, 2016, about four months after the last component went in[296](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=296)[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=297) .
- **Adakveo (crizanlizumab-tmca), BLA 761128.** BTD was granted December 20, 2018, and rolling review February 7, 2019. The last of six BLA submissions arrived May 16, 2019. The Priority review ended in a decision on November 15, 2019[293](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=293) .
- **Imbruvica (ibrutinib), NDA 205552.** Fast Track was granted October 2012 and BTD March 2013. FDA granted rolling review April 18, 2013, and the three NDA parts arrived April 25, May 31, and June 28, 2013. The record is Priority. The June 2013 NDA covered two indications and was administratively split: mantle-cell lymphoma (Original 1) was approved November 13, 2013, and CLL (Original 2) on February 12, 2014. The cited review[304](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=304) is the Original 2 (CLL) review.
- **Praxbind (idarucizumab), BLA 761025.** This BTD product had its rolling BLA completed February 20, 2015. The Priority review ended in a decision on October 16, 2015[298](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=298) .


The review files cited here do not state PDUFA goal dates, so they cannot show how these approvals compared with their goals. Cumulatively, CDER reports 337 breakthrough therapy approvals as of December 31, 2025[111](https://www.fda.gov/media/95302/download) . In calendar 2025, 15 of CDER's 46 novel approvals had BTD[109](https://www.fda.gov/media/190705/download) .


### RMAT: breakthrough-level engagement for regenerative medicine


RMAT guidance is in *Expedited Programs for Regenerative Medicine Therapies for Serious Conditions* (February 2019)[90](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=90) . The main difference from BTD is the evidentiary trigger. RMAT requires preliminary clinical evidence of potential to address an unmet medical need. It does not require evidence of substantial improvement over available therapy[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=85)[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=84) .


CBER will also accept a wider range of preliminary evidence:


- appropriately chosen historical controls,
- well-designed retrospective studies,
- case series with systematically collected data, and
- studies conducted outside the United States[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=47) .


Once designated, an RMAT product gets every BTD feature (and so every Fast Track feature)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=29) . It also gets early interactions on surrogate or intermediate endpoints that could support accelerated approval[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=47)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=29) . The statute also directs attention to ways of supporting accelerated approval and meeting postapproval requirements[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=29) . Like BTD, RMAT is not an approval and does not change the safety and effectiveness standard[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=84) .


**Precedents.** Through FY2025 (September 30, 2025), FDA received 388 RMAT requests and granted 193[64](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/cellular-gene-therapy-products/cumulative-cber-regenerative-medicine-advanced-therapy-rmat-designation-requests-received-fiscal) . It lists 14 approved products that held RMAT designation, including Casgevy, Zevaskyn, Aucatzyl, Tecelra, Lenmeldy, Amtagvi, Roctavian, and Breyanzi[71](https://www.fda.gov/vaccines-blood-biologics/cellular-gene-therapy-products/cber-regenerative-medicine-advanced-therapy-rmat-approvals) . Two regulatory histories show how RMAT combines with other programs:


- **Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel).** RMAT was granted May 5, 2020, alongside Fast Track, Orphan, and Priority Review. The BLA arrived April 3, 2023, was filed June 8, 2023, and was approved December 8, 2023[378](https://www.fda.gov/media/175179/download?attachment=) . That is six months after filing, in line with the priority goal for original BLAs, which runs from the 60-day filing date[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=269) .
- **Otarmeni (lunsotogene parvec-cwha).** RMAT was granted July 5, 2024. The product also held Fast Track, Orphan, Priority Review, and accelerated approval, and it was reviewed under the CNPV pilot. The complete BLA arrived December 23, 2025, was filed with priority review February 21, 2026, and was approved April 23, 2026[380](https://www.fda.gov/media/192364/download) .


### Priority Review: the only program that changes the review clock


Priority review changes how long FDA takes to act. It does not change the approval pathway or the evidence needed. Under the PDUFA goals, FDA aims to act on 90% of applications within these windows[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=269) :


Application type Priority Standard


NME NDAs and original BLAs ("the Program") 6 months from the 60-day filing date (about 8 months from receipt) 10 months from the 60-day filing date (about 12 months from receipt)


Non-NME original NDAs 6 months from receipt 10 months from receipt


"Act" means issuing either an approval or a complete response letter. Meeting the goal does not mean approval[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=269) . FDA decides priority status case by case at filing and tells the applicant by day 60[268](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=268)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31)[271](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=271) .


The clock can move. **Palynziq (pegvaliase-pqpz), BLA 761079** was received June 30, 2017 under priority review. A major amendment then extended the review by three months, to a PDUFA goal of May 28, 2018. FDA acted May 24, 2018[351](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=351) .


**How often priority review is used.** Drugs@FDA approval-letter records for original applications classified as new molecular entities show this split (example records:[115](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=115)[116](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=116)[117](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=117)[118](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=118)[119](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=119)[120](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=120)[121](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=121)[122](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=122) ):


Year Priority Standard


2023 33 22


2024 29 22


2025 25 22


These are counts of original applications, not products, so a product approved under two applications (lenacapavir in 2025, for example) counts twice and yearly totals can exceed CDER's novel-approval counts.


The designations stack. A product with Fast Track or BTD commonly also gets priority review at filing, as the Cabometyx, Adakveo, and Casgevy records show[296](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=296)[293](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=293)[378](https://www.fda.gov/media/175179/download?attachment=) .


### Where accelerated approval fits


Accelerated approval is an approval pathway, not a designation. It lets FDA approve on a surrogate or intermediate clinical endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit, for a serious condition where the product offers a meaningful advantage over available therapy[10](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=10)[5](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=5)[7](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=7) . The statutory standards stay the same, and confirmatory trials must verify the benefit[3](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=3)[10](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=10) .


Congress tightened the pathway in section 3210 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023[22](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=22)[51](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=51) . FDA's draft guidances from December 2024 and January 2025 cover the resulting changes:


- FDA generally intends to require confirmatory trials to be underway before approval, and may require enrollment to be complete in some cases[369](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=369)[12](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=12) .
- Sponsors must submit progress reports roughly every 180 days[12](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=12) .
- FDA can use expedited withdrawal procedures if a trial is not run with due diligence or fails to confirm benefit[370](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=370)[372](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=372)[373](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=373) .


This affects BTD and RMAT planning. The early discussions on surrogate endpoints that those designations support now need to cover confirmatory trial readiness too.


### Commissioner's National Priority Voucher: a different kind of acceleration


#### Mechanics


FDA announced the CNPV pilot on June 17, 2025[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests) . It covers CDER, CBER, and the Oncology Center of Excellence[75](https://www.fda.gov/media/190896/download)[78](https://www.fda.gov/media/190927/download) . The target is an action within 1 to 2 months after the final application is submitted, compared with roughly 10 to 12 months for a standard review[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests)[74](https://www.fda.gov/industry/commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program)[76](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-schedules-public-meeting-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-pilot-program) .


The program saves time by removing idle periods. It does not reduce the amount of review:


- **Pre-submission.** CMC and draft labeling are due at least 60 days before the final submission, and other modules follow an agreed schedule[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests)[75](https://www.fda.gov/media/190896/download) .
- **Ongoing communication.** Sponsors are expected to answer FDA questions quickly. Early engagement is meant to catch CMC, inspection, and labeling problems before they extend the review[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests)[76](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-schedules-public-meeting-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-pilot-program)[83](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-grants-two-national-priority-vouchers) .
- **Tumor-board review.** The center's review team still does the independent scientific review. It then presents its findings to a multidisciplinary CNPV Review Council at a one-day meeting. The Council's recommendations are non-binding, and the product center keeps approval authority[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests)[75](https://www.fda.gov/media/190896/download)[78](https://www.fda.gov/media/190927/download)[74](https://www.fda.gov/industry/commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program) .


FDA's February 2026 town hall described an illustrative schedule: a 60-day pre-submission period, a 14 to 21 day filing period, and a 30 to 60 day review[78](https://www.fda.gov/media/190927/download) . Vouchers cannot be transferred[74](https://www.fda.gov/industry/commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program)[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests) . The approval standard does not change, a voucher does not make approval more likely, and FDA can extend the timeline for incomplete data, ambiguous pivotal results, manufacturing problems, or complex reviews[74](https://www.fda.gov/industry/commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program)[75](https://www.fda.gov/media/190896/download)[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests)[79](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-awards-first-ever-national-priority-vouchers-nine-sponsors) .


#### Recipients and outcomes


- **Vouchers.** FDA named nine recipients on October 16, 2025 and six more on November 6, 2025. With later awards in December, the total reached 18 by December 19, 2025[79](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-awards-first-ever-national-priority-vouchers-nine-sponsors)[80](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-awards-second-batch-national-priority-vouchers)[81](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-proactively-awards-national-priority-voucher-based-strong-phase-3-study-results)[83](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-grants-two-national-priority-vouchers) .
- **2026 awards.** On April 24, 2026, FDA announced three more vouchers, for psilocybin and methylone programs in depression and PTSD[414](https://psychedelicalpha.com/news/breaking-fda-awards-priority-review-vouchers-to-otsuka-compass-and-usona/)[418](https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/compass-usona-score-fda-national-priority-vouchers-amid-trump-administrations-psychedelic) .
- **Status in April 2026.** At the Foundayo approval on April 1, 2026, FDA reported 18 vouchers awarded and six CNPV decisions issued[416](https://crwepressrelease.com/press-release/12402/fda-approves-first-new-molecular-entity-under-national-priority-voucher-program) .

A voucher does not guarantee approval. Bitopertin was in the first group of recipients, but it received a complete response letter on February 13, 2026, after about four months of review[59](https://pharmadossier.com/blog/fda-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program) .


Two points matter when comparing these timelines with PDUFA goals:


- The 1 to 2 month target starts at filing or final submission. The Otarmeni history shows a two-month gap between receipt and filing[380](https://www.fda.gov/media/192364/download) .
- Much of the CMC and labeling review happens during the 60-day pre-submission window[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests)[78](https://www.fda.gov/media/190927/download) .


#### Open issues


CNPV has no dedicated statute. FDA's March 23, 2026 *Federal Register* notice, which announced a public hearing and requested comments, relies on FDA's general authority under the FD&C Act and PHS Act[327](https://www.citizen.org/article/comments-to-the-fda-about-the-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-pilot-program/) . In January 2026 FDA also issued a staff manual guide describing who makes decisions under the program[60](https://www.biospace.com/fda/9-months-in-fdas-new-priority-voucher-program-still-clouded-with-uncertainty) . As of March 2026, FDA had issued no guidance document defining the program[327](https://www.citizen.org/article/comments-to-the-fda-about-the-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-pilot-program/)[60](https://www.biospace.com/fda/9-months-in-fdas-new-priority-voucher-program-still-clouded-with-uncertainty) .


Critics have raised several concerns:


- the lack of explicit statutory authority[327](https://www.citizen.org/article/comments-to-the-fda-about-the-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-pilot-program/)[329](https://hlc.com/en/publications/fda-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-program-comes-with-questions-surrounding-implementation)[331](https://www.americanactionforum.org/insight/assessing-the-fdas-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-program/) ;
- vague selection criteria that mix clinical and industrial-policy goals (onshoring, pricing)[327](https://www.citizen.org/article/comments-to-the-fda-about-the-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-pilot-program/)[331](https://www.americanactionforum.org/insight/assessing-the-fdas-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-program/)[333](https://petrieflom.law.harvard.edu/2026/03/13/hazards-ahead-for-fdas-drug-review-process/) ;
- the risk of political influence on product selection[327](https://www.citizen.org/article/comments-to-the-fda-about-the-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-pilot-program/)[328](https://www.americanactionforum.org/weekly-checkup/whither-the-fdas-commissioners-national-priority-voucher/)[332](https://apnews.com/article/fda-makary-drug-voucher-program-29d830175911c3c7432616385a421a2c) ;
- diversion of reviewers from non-CNPV applications that are working to PDUFA goals[328](https://www.americanactionforum.org/weekly-checkup/whither-the-fdas-commissioners-national-priority-voucher/)[329](https://hlc.com/en/publications/fda-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-program-comes-with-questions-surrounding-implementation)[331](https://www.americanactionforum.org/insight/assessing-the-fdas-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-program/) ;
- less time to work through safety signals and complex data[327](https://www.citizen.org/article/comments-to-the-fda-about-the-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-pilot-program/)[328](https://www.americanactionforum.org/weekly-checkup/whither-the-fdas-commissioners-national-priority-voucher/)[331](https://www.americanactionforum.org/insight/assessing-the-fdas-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-program/) .


### Practical implications for sponsors


- **Choose by development stage.** Fast Track is available on nonclinical or mechanistic data and mainly buys access to FDA[28](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=28)[36](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=36) . BTD and RMAT pay off most when requested before the pivotal trials, because their main value is FDA input on trial design[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=38)[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31)[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=84) .
- **Choose RMAT over BTD where eligible.** For cell and gene therapies without head-to-head evidence, RMAT gives the same engagement without the substantial-improvement showing[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=85)[84](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=84) .
- **Plan the clock around filing.** For NMEs and original BLAs, the priority goal runs 6 months from the 60-day filing date[269](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=269) . Major amendments can add three months, as Palynziq shows[351](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=351) . Rolling review can shorten the gap between data lock and action, as in Cabometyx[296](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=296)[297](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=297) .
- **Treat designations as revocable.** FDA can rescind Fast Track, BTD, and RMAT as the evidence or the treatment landscape changes[31](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=31)[38](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=38)[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=41)[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=321)[29](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fast-track-vs-breakthrough-therapy-vs-rmat?showSourceNumber=29) .
- **For CNPV, be submission-ready before you ask.** The pilot depends on CMC and labeling being ready 60 days before final submission, and on fast sponsor responses[77](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-issue-new-commissioners-national-priority-vouchers-companies-supporting-us-national-interests)[75](https://www.fda.gov/media/190896/download) . Readiness is also a selection criterion[75](https://www.fda.gov/media/190896/download)[78](https://www.fda.gov/media/190927/download) . The bitopertin complete response shows that speed does not substitute for a clean dossier[59](https://pharmadossier.com/blog/fda-commissioners-national-priority-voucher-cnpv-pilot-program) .
